long_biography.plain_text:
Keith Lloyd was an Australian pioneer of large-vessel construction. The Brisbane yard he founded built aluminium craft for private and commercial use, becoming a prominent Australian builder of large motor vessels. He ultimately sold the business to entrepreneur Christopher Skase.

Lloyd remained a source of practical marine knowledge after the sale. He advised prospective charter operators on running costs and consulted with Benetti during construction of an award-winning motor vessel in Italy. A Federal Court judgment later recorded his advice on operating costs and described his company as one of Australia's most prestigious specialist boatbuilders.

uncertainties.detail: The input's exact name, Australian profile and Southern Cross II relationship match direct 2020 reporting about Brisbane shipbuilder Keith Lloyd. Later maritime reporting states that he sold the vessel in 2021 and died in 2023, so the source record's current-ownership and Alive values are stale. Those changes do not undermine the identity match.

Several independent reports establish that Lloyd died in 2023 aged 85, and estate reporting narrows this to November. A detailed local memorial gives 26 November 2023, documenting a complete death date while the inventory treats death-date fields as system-managed rather than researchable. Age 85 permits two possible birth years depending on his birthday, so no birth day, month or year is inferred.

The founder-built and later sold shipyard is the earliest documented substantial business and is therefore classified as the inferred wealth-creation sector. Lloyd later owned an international college and substantial property, but sources do not quantify their contributions or establish the dominant sector at death. Manufacturing is used for primary industry only as the disclosed origin-sector fallback.

Brisbane Times identified Cameron Lloyd as Keith Lloyd's son and a Shafston College director in 2011. That management role does not establish that Cameron or another child received a family stake, and later sources describe an ownership transition around 2021 without documenting a transfer to Lloyd's family. No inheritance, family-transfer or heir relationship is inferred from surname, directorship or estate beneficiaries.

Founder accurately describes Lloyd's historical relationship to the shipyard and college, but the shipyard was sold, he left college management, and the education and property holdings changed hands before his death. Public reports of his estate do not establish one continuing principal business or investment role, so the current wealth relationship remains Unknown.

Focused searches of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok and personal-web contexts returned many unrelated Keith Lloyd profiles but no exact-person account meeting the identity threshold. The current Shafston website represents a successor-owned institution and is not proposed as Lloyd's company website.
No dedicated Forbes profile or exact-person Forbes result was found. The only prominent Forbes result concerned an unrelated Dunlop racket-sports product manager named Keith Lloyd.

Shipbuilding is the minimum useful approved tag because Lloyd founded and controlled a substantial yard serving both luxury and commercial markets. Superyacht construction was considered but omitted as a narrower overlapping cohort, while commercial shipowner and shipping-operation tags would confuse construction with fleet ownership. International education is preserved in the biography because no precise active catalogue assignment was identified.

review.notes:
Terminal research decision: Keith Lloyd resolves at very high confidence as the late Australian founder of Lloyd Ships and Shafston International College. Direct owner-context reporting links him to the exact source vessel, while maritime, court, education, property and estate sources converge on the same Brisbane entrepreneur. The input's Alive value is corrected to Deceased; 26 November 2023 is documented in the research context but not proposed because the inventory treats death-date fields as system-managed. Gender, known-for title and biography are also supported. Manufacturing is the reasoned creation sector, broad Self-made is supported by founder-built enterprises, and Manufacturing is retained for primary industry only as the required origin-sector fallback. Wealth relationship remains Unknown because the historical founder assets were sold or transitioned before his death. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Shipbuilding: assigned because Lloyd founded and controlled a substantial aluminium yard and remained publicly identified with Australian large-yacht construction. [2] Superyacht construction: omitted as a narrower overlapping tag because the yard also built commercial vessels and the broader Shipbuilding cohort best represents his defining industrial role. [3] Commercial shipowner and shipping-operation tags: omitted because construction and ownership of personal yachts do not establish a defining commercial-fleet role. [4] International education: defining biography material through Shafston College, but no precise active catalogue assignment was identified. The approved minimum useful tag set is Shipbuilding only.
